differences.what: A states the gate maps the coefficient check relies on, for both constructions: copy, side injection (sum over |S∩T|=1, and -sum (|S∩T|-1)/2 A_ST in the complex case), gather (with C_* in the complex case) and scatter ((sum C_i - C_*)/2). It also lists the eight-row schedule. B gives only the neighbour relations and the resulting coefficients.

items.note: B1-B4 are present in both (A K1.4-K1.6; B S1.1.1a-c, S1.1.2), as are the wire counts. A also carries the construction maps from which the central and side coefficients follow.

differences.what: B states the proof's invariant: the stored array equals D_v applied to the logical array, it holds at the sources by defining g=D_in^{-1}f with no preprocessing, and each edge carries D_u phi to D_v phi. A gives only the gate commutation and the resulting operator.

items.note: Both state commutation with pointwise gates, D_out S D_in^{-1} and the route operator. Only B carries the invariant argument that proves them.

differences.what: B lists the residual table as subspaces with dimensions (B⊗t_X^⊥, P⊗t_X^⊥, B⊗F, P⊗F, B⊗<t_Y>, (B⊗t_Y^⊥)⊥(P⊗<t_X>), P⊗<t_X,t_Y>^⊥, P⊗<t_Y>, (A⊗F)⊗Q^⊥). A lists only the dimensions.
B shows why stage labels fit together (A'=A⊗F, P'=P⊗<t>, B'=(P')^⊥_{A'}, starting at U_a,0 and ending at F,U_a^⊥). A only asserts that they match.

items.note: L2-L5 are present in both: A K3.4 and the K3 motivation, K3.2, K3.5-K3.7; B S1.3.5d, S1.3.2, S1.3.6-S1.3.8. L1 is complete only in B, where the residuals themselves are listed and not just their dimensions.

Both assign P_U, -P_{U_a} and zero. Both show that rank(P_V-P_U) equals the dimension change, the N exceptional 2P_{U_a} source edges, s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b with deficit N-2L_b>0, and endpoint difference I_m (A K4.1-K4.3; B S1.4.1a-c).

differences.what: On k columns each residual vector contributes one tensored factor, s_c factors in all, stated in the interface. B gives the total s_c but never the k-column tensor statement in this role.
Endpoint frames: the zero label has frame I and the full label C^{⊗m}. A states this. B only says the X_a->Y_a route is the one whose labels are neither zero nor full.
B derives the X_a->Y_a phase difference q_{U_a^⊥}-q_{U_a}=wt(x)+2[u·x] mod 4, which yields C^{-1} on supp(u_a). A states only the result.

items.note: P1 and P2 are present in both. P3 and the endpoint-frame part of P4 are carried by A only. B's explicit phase-difference formula only partly offsets this.

R1-R4 are present in both: L/N<1/2 with deficits N-2L_b and 2N-2L_c, both eta values, both deficits >20·2^{-50}, log m<20, and s/W<m^tau with tau=sigma=1-2^{-50} (A K3.7, K4.2, K5.2, K6; B S1.3.8, S1.4.1b, S1.4.2b, S1.4.3a-c).

differences.what: A states both linear-cost lemmas: the elementary stream operations, including the cyclic row split into W streams, and controlled shifts y->y+a(controls) mod q^b with b^{O(1)} offset preparation, plus fixed rational unit scalings. B has no step that states either lemma; it only uses them.

items.note: B relies on tape-stream-operations and controlled-shift but never states their content. A carries both lemmas with their conditions.

differences.what: Elimination proof: B gives the A=0 case, the iteration that deletes the pivot row and column and repeats on the active indices (still lower triangular, earlier pivots untouched), and E_1=L^{-1}, E_2=R^{-1}. A gives only the pivot rule and lower-triangular clearing.

items.note: M2-M4 are present in both (A C2.1-C2.3; B S1.5.2a-c). M1 is complete only in B.

Both carry: the cyclic row split into W streams of volume V/W, the Phi_{A_e} edge shears by recursive interchanges, H<-H+D on every row, the three-update interchange, s calls giving F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1) and F_k=O(e^tau), and the depth-first schedule with descriptor bound (A C3.1-C3.6; B S1.5.3.1-S1.5.3.5d).

differences.what: Chunks whose widths differ by one bit: B moves the extra leading bit outside the equal-width pair at one extra O(V) single-bit move. A omits this case.
B describes exchanging the top rho digits digit by digit and joining them, at cost O(V rho), to form the row field. A only says the high digits serve as the row field.

items.note: Both give k, rho, R=q^{2rho}>=W^k, padding to R'<2R, the base-m split with O(V e^tau) cost, and padding to [q^e]. B adds the unequal-width case and the high-digit movement.

Both give: the C identities, the P_M conjugation with residual-basis columns, slot-wise children with (C^{-1})^{⊗f}=(-i)^f Z C Z, at most m(m-1)+3m row additions, exactly s_c children, and H_0^{⊗D}=b^D S_D C^{⊗D} S_D (A L1.1-L1.6; B S1.6.1a-f).

Both give: the eight-update parity cycles, the single cyclic shift per line, the guard set with 20 excluded values and delta_bad, T_0S_0^{-1} permuting the bad set, repair by sorting, the top position handled separately, the cost terms, and the use for a change of basis (A P1-P6; B S1.6.2a-i).

Both give: individual kernels O(Ve), s children with O(V((eK)^tau+1)) overhead, q_0 rows and padding, the 1/W volume per role, the exponent conditions, internal O(e^lambda), leaves O(e^sigma d^{beta(1-sigma)}), and base-m pieces giving O(d^{lambda'}) (A B1-B6; B S1.6.3a-g).

S1-S5 are present in both: the constants E, B, nu=11, C_1=20, C_0, Delta; A(e)<=sA(e/m)+E with the per-invocation count below E; unrolling to 8B^2d^{nu+1} and the total below C_0d^{C_1}; depth-ell values with the bit reservation and Delta=o(p); and the absolute row sum one (A L4, GB1-GB6, L6; B S1.6.4a-f, S1.6.5b).

differences.what: B's layout method says the 'top bit slots of each axis (at most D(b+1))' go to the prefix. The paper moves the top slot of each long axis and the low slots h=b-1..0. B's S2.3a states this correctly.
B prices each prefix-slot round at O(Tp). The paper's O(Tp) is per participating bit, at most D per round, and gives O(TpdK) in total.
B gives the round order: h=l-1 on the long axes, then the qK chunk rounds, then the bottom positions.

items.note: Otherwise the contents match: contractions, character cancellation, decimation in frequency, bit-reversed storage, round grouping, layout cost and error. B's two minor misstatements in the layout step tip this to A.

differences.what: B gives the signed encoding of A_u: digits d_j=u_j+gamma_j mod B_0 with carries gamma in {-1,0}, a two's-complement block encoding, gamma_r=-1 exactly for negative A_u, in O(rp). A only says the polynomials are packed.

items.note: Both give B_0=2^{4p}, the 4pr-bit bound, the separation |h_j|<B_0/2, centred-residue extraction, reduction mod y^r+1 and the O(rp log(rp)) cost. B adds the packing step.
Both give F^-(f*g)=M(F^-f)(F^-g), F^+F^-=I/M, P(LBu,LBv)=LBP(u,v), the error 2delta+eta, then 3delta+eta, then M(3delta+eta), and the log(rp) cost term (A R7-R8; B S2.5a-c).

differences.what: Why A and B_0 are contractions: ||S'||<3/4, ||J'||<7/8, ||D'||<1 and ||C||=1. A asserts contractions without these bounds.
The condition for invertibility: alpha^2 < p and theta > p/alpha^4 give alpha^2 theta > 1, hence ||N-I||<1/2. A states ||N-I||<1/2 without the reason.
Definitions of S, T, the selection C and the diagonal D, with N=CTD having unit diagonal.
The O(p)-per-index generation of the selected indices, and the Neumann evaluation of J' with its O(tp sqrt(p) alpha) cost.

items.note: Both carry the left-inverse identity, the normalizations 2^{-2alpha^2}, the error and time table, the unexecuted sorts and the tensor and exposure costs. B alone supplies the contraction and invertibility justifications and the implementation details.
Both give the chirp coefficient check for QF_t and the unit-dilation argument RF^+R=F^+ leading to (u*v)/S^2, with conjugation for RF^+ (A G2-G3; B S3.3, S3.4a-b).

differences.what: B checks the prime-interval hypothesis x>e^{2/eta}: log(r/2)/d -> infinity, so log x > 8d = 2/eta for x=r/2 and x=r. B also notes gcd(s_i,t_i)=1 because t_i is a power of two. A states the cited bound but not this check.

items.note: The fixed rationals, sizes, bands, alpha and gamma, prime count, Bernoulli bound, alpha^4 theta_i>p, the search cost and the no-wraparound and capacity bounds are in both. B adds the hypothesis check.
Both give: the isomorphism, the triangular formula, padding, the update order i=d..1 with interval rotations preserving the padding, and the O(d^2) axis reversal cost (A CR1-CR4; B S5.1a-e).
Both give: well-definedness, diagonal isometry, wrap-sign cancellation, M_C=D_- iota^{-1} M_r(iota D_+ ., iota D_+ .)=(f*g)/T, and the computed twist (A PT1-PT3; B S5.2a-c).

Both give the computed chirp transform and source transform with their exact counterparts, the conjugated opposite procedure, the six-step algorithm, and the two S scalings undoing (u*v)/S^2 (A S5.6-S5.7; B S5.3-S5.4).
Both chain E_ring<5TL, 6TL, 8TL, E_s=9·2^gamma TL and E_w<28·2^gamma T^2 L to the final bound below 1/2, then rounding and carries (A ER1-ER6; B S5.5a-j).

Both give: the cost table, margins g_1..g_7 with min 2^{-181}=2kappa, row derivations, o(V) setup and exceptional sorting, absorption of log p powers, and the schoolbook cutoff (A T1-T5; B S6.1-S6.6).
Both state the eventual lower bound, its negation by a liminf of zero, and that the bound gives a limit of zero (A S1; B S7).

chain.note: Both trees follow the paper's route. The three-stage exchange network, frames and nested labels give s_b and s_c below Wm. From there s/W<m^tau with tau=sigma=1-2^{-50}, which drives the interchange recurrence F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1) and the layer recurrence F(e)<=(s/W)F(e/m)+.... These feed the synthetic transforms and the convolution, and the cost table's margin g_2=epsilon c(1-tau) gives O(n(lg n)^{1-kappa}). Neither chain breaks where the other holds; their dependencies match the paper's.

errors.says: The layout moves 'the top bit slots of each axis (at most D(b+1) of them) to a prefix'.
errors.paper: The prefix receives the top slot (i,l-1) of each long axis and the low slots (i,h), h=b-1..0, of every axis. B's own S2.3a states this correctly.

errors.says: Each prefix-slot round halves a bit individually at O(Tp) per round.
errors.paper: The bits of a prefix round are processed individually, O(Tp) for the moves and scans of each bit (up to D per round), for O(TpdK) over at most K rounds.

overall.reason: Neither plan has a major error, and both carry the central saving chain completely and faithfully. A is more complete on the complex phase interface (P3, and P4's endpoint frames I and C^{⊗m}) and alone states the stream and controlled-shift lemmas; B has two minor slips in the layout step. B is more complete on the residual table (L1), the elimination proof (M1), the resampling contraction and invertibility justifications, unequal-width interchange, signed packing and the prime-interval check. On the checklist the sub-step differences balance (P3, P4 against L1, M1), and the remaining differences are completeness details pointing both ways, so neither set clearly outweighs the other.
